name: a(n) is the smallest integer k > 2*n such that Product_{i=1..n} (k - i) has no prime factor p in n < p < 2*n.
comment: Erdős asks for an estimation of k (see Erdős Problems link).
link: William Alexander Carney, Table of n, a(n) for n = 1..209 (terms 1..70 from _Giorgos Kalogeropoulos_, terms 71..92 from _Chai Wah Wu_, terms 93..183 from _Charles R Greathouse IV_)
William Alexander Carney, C++ program (exact residue-class search over the primes in (n,2n) with per-n minimality proof)
William Alexander Carney, Python driver for the C++ search (checkpointing and reproduction gate against the published terms)
Wouter van Doorn and Quanyu Tang, Consecutive integers free of certain prime factors, arXiv:2606.19863 [math.NT], 2026.
formula: van Doorn & Tang prove that a(n) > exp(log^2 n/20 log log n) for large enough n. - _Charles R Greathouse IV_, Jun 22 2026
Trivial upper bound: a(n) < exp((1 + o(1))*n) by the PNT. - _Charles R Greathouse IV_, Jun 26 2026
example: For n = 5 the smallest k > 10 such that (k-1)*(k-2)..(k-5) has no prime factor in (5, 10) is k = 13.
program: (PARI) isok(k, n) = for (i=1, n, my(f=factor(k-i)[,1]); for (j=1, #f~, if ((f[j]>n) && (f[j]<2*n), return(0)))); return(1);
a(n) = my(k=2*n+1); while(!isok(k, n), k++); k; \\ _Michel Marcus_, Oct 23 2025
(PARI) a(k)=my(L=vecprod(primes([k+1,2*k-1])),n=2*k+1); while(1, for(i=1,k, if(gcd(n-i,L)>1, n+=k+1-i; next(2))); return(n)) \\ _Charles R Greathouse IV_, Jun 22 2026
